description: Canonical terms for the Valmet 2018–2022 LCA expert assessment report.

keywords.short: A source-grounded professional assessment of LCA readiness and disclosure usefulness.
keywords.definition: In this report, LCA expert assessment means using professional LCA questions to evaluate what Valmet's public disclosures can and cannot support, with every finding traced to Evidence Objects.

keywords.short: The sequence of LCA questions that drives evidence collection and diagnosis.
keywords.definition: The question chain starts from corporate inventory, Scope 3 hotspots, product LCA readiness, value-chain leverage, assurance and targets, then iterates based on missing evidence.

keywords.short: A loop of expert question, ontology extraction, evidence judgement, missing-field flagging and ontology refinement.
keywords.definition: This report uses ontology extraction as the evidence layer in an iterative LCA review process: expert questions define evidence needs, extraction produces Evidence Objects, audit flags expose gaps, and the ontology is refined for the next round.
An Evidence Object stores concept type, canonical concept, value, unit, year, source file, page, quote, applicability, missing fields, audit flags and review status.

keywords.short: A professional diagnostic claim linked to Evidence Object IDs.
keywords.definition: A finding is evidence-backed only when its claim, LCA implication and recommendation can be traced to specific Evidence Objects with source quotes and pages.

keywords.short: How usable the disclosures are for corporate GHG inventory review.
keywords.definition: A readiness assessment for company-level GHG inventory and disclosure trend analysis. It does not imply product-level LCA readiness.

keywords.short: Using Scope 3 category evidence to identify likely priority areas.
keywords.definition: The Valmet assessment uses Category 1/4/6/9 Evidence Objects to identify purchased goods and services as the dominant captured Scope 3 hotspot.

keywords.short: Whether evidence is sufficient for product-level LCA modelling.
keywords.definition: Product LCA readiness requires functional unit, product system boundary, foreground flows, allocation, method and source-grounded values. This Valmet case is rated low because those elements are missing from public disclosures.

keywords.short: Audit flag for missing calculation-method detail.
keywords.definition: An audit flag indicating that a row has values and units but lacks enough emission-factor, activity-data or calculation-method detail for direct LCI reuse.

keywords.short: The quantified reference unit of a product LCA study.
keywords.definition: Functional unit defines the quantified performance basis for product LCA. The extracted Valmet LCA/use-phase claims do not provide a functional unit, blocking product-LCA-ready interpretation.

keywords.short: The environmental influence created when Valmet technologies affect customer-site operations.
keywords.definition: For Valmet, customer use-phase leverage captures the idea that major value-chain environmental impacts may occur when customers use Valmet technologies in production, so LCA interpretation must model customer-site scenarios rather than only own operations.

keywords.short: A Finnish listed process-industry technology, automation and services company.
keywords.definition: In this report, Valmet is treated as a B2B process-industry technology and lifecycle service company whose environmental relevance spans own operations, supply chain and customer use phase.

keywords.short: The next evidence layer needed to move from Scope 3 screening to LCA modelling.
keywords.definition: For Valmet, supplier/material data would connect Category 1 purchased goods and services to material composition, activity quantities, supplier-specific factors and emission-factor provenance.
